main.claim: Open the webcam test, allow camera access, and you see yourself live in your browser. It shows the resolution and frame rate your camera reports, lets you switch cameras, and saves a PNG snapshot. Free, no app, nothing uploaded.

sections.heading: How to test your webcam
sections.body:
Open [Webcam Test](https://webcam-test.lazur.app/) in the browser you use for calls. When the page asks, select Allow for the camera. Your live picture appears within a few seconds. If you can see yourself, the camera works in that browser.

1. Open [Webcam Test](https://webcam-test.lazur.app/).
2. Select Allow when the browser asks for the camera.
3. Look at the live picture and check the framing, the light and the focus.
4. If you have more than one camera, open the camera list and pick the one you want to check.

The picture is mirrored, the way a mirror shows you. When you move your right hand, it moves on the right side of the picture. That makes it easier to line yourself up for a call.

sections.heading: What the resolution and frame rate mean
sections.body:
The page shows the resolution and frame rate that your camera reports to the browser. Resolution is how many pixels the picture has across and down, such as 1280 by 720 or 1920 by 1080. Frame rate is how many pictures the camera sends each second, written as FPS. A higher resolution keeps fine detail sharp. A higher frame rate makes movement look smooth.

These numbers show what the camera reports. They do not show how a video app will send your picture to other people. Your app may lower the quality when your internet connection is slow. Use the numbers as a check that the camera is working, and judge the picture itself for the rest.

**Look at the picture, not only the numbers.** A picture that is dark, soft or frozen when you move will look worse on a call, even when the numbers look high.

sections.heading: Fix a black or frozen picture
sections.body:
If the picture is black, or it never appears, work through these checks:

- Select Allow when the browser asks for the camera. If you blocked it once, allow it in your browser's site settings, then reload the page.
- Close other apps that may use the camera, such as a video call app, a camera app or a browser tab on a meeting site.
- Check that nothing covers the lens. Some laptops have a physical shutter, or a key that turns the camera off.
- On a computer, check that the camera is allowed in the system settings. The steps are on the pages for [Windows 11](https://webcam-test.lazur.app/windows-11) and [Chromebook](https://webcam-test.lazur.app/chromebook).

After each change, reload the page and look at the live picture again.

sections.heading: Take a snapshot to check framing
sections.body:
Select the snapshot button to save a still image of your picture as a PNG file, then download it. A snapshot is a quick way to check framing: where your head sits in the frame, how much of the room shows and how the light falls on your face. Take one from the spot where you plan to sit, then compare it with the picture you want on the call.

The test takes still snapshots, not video clips. To see how your video looks in motion, use the preview in your video app, as described on the pages for [Zoom](https://webcam-test.lazur.app/zoom) and [Teams](https://webcam-test.lazur.app/camera-teams).

sections.heading: What happens to your video
sections.body:
The test runs in your browser. The live picture and snapshots stay on your device, and nothing is uploaded. You do not need to install an app or create an account. When you close the page, the live picture stops.

If you also want to check your microphone, open [Mic Test](https://mic-test.lazur.app/) in the same browser.

pages.title: Webcam Test for Laptop: Check Your Laptop Camera Free | Lazur
pages.description: Check your laptop camera in the browser with a live picture, the resolution and frame rate it reports, and a snapshot. Free, no sign-up needed.
pages.claim: Open the webcam test on your laptop, allow the camera, and the live picture appears in your browser. It shows the resolution and frame rate the camera reports, and you can save a snapshot. Free, no app, nothing uploaded.

sections.heading: Check your laptop camera in four steps
sections.body:
Run this check before a meeting, while you sit in the spot you will use on the call.

1. Open the [webcam test](https://webcam-test.lazur.app/laptop) in your laptop's browser.
2. Select Allow when the browser asks for the camera.
3. Look at the live picture. It is mirrored, so it matches what you see in a mirror.
4. Check the resolution and frame rate the page reports, then take a snapshot if you want a still image to compare.

If you see yourself, the camera works in this browser. Keep the laptop in the same place and at the same height as on the call, so the framing you check is the framing other people will see.

sections.heading: Choose the right camera
sections.body:
Most laptops have one built-in camera. If you plug in a USB webcam, the page can list both. Open the camera list and pick the one you plan to use on the call. The live picture switches to that camera, so you can compare the two by changing the choice.

The list shows the cameras the browser can see right now. If the camera you want is missing, unplug it, plug it back in and reload the page. Once you have picked a camera, choose the same one in your meeting app too. This test only sets the camera for this browser, so the app needs its own check.

sections.heading: If the laptop camera is black
sections.body:
A black picture usually means one of three things: another app is using the camera, the browser is not allowed to use it, or the lens is covered or the camera is switched off. Close video call apps and any meeting tabs in other browser windows, then reload this page. Check the browser prompt again and select Allow.

Look at the laptop itself for a shutter or a cover over the lens. Some laptops also have a key that switches the camera off. On Windows, the steps for checking the camera in Settings are on the [Windows 11 page](https://webcam-test.lazur.app/windows-11). On a Chromebook, see the [Chromebook page](https://webcam-test.lazur.app/chromebook).

sections.heading: What this check does not cover
sections.body:
This test shows that your laptop camera sends a live picture to the browser. It does not check your microphone, and it does not show how a video app will display you. For a meeting, run the app's own check as well. Zoom has one in its Video & effects settings, and Microsoft Teams has a test call in its Devices settings.

Use the [Zoom page](https://webcam-test.lazur.app/zoom) or the [Teams page](https://webcam-test.lazur.app/camera-teams) for those steps.

faq.q: How do I test my laptop camera before a meeting?
faq.a: Open the webcam test in your laptop's browser, select Allow when it asks for the camera, and check the live picture. Then open your meeting app's own camera preview, because the app may use a different camera. If both show a clear picture from the same camera, you are ready.

faq.q: How do I test that my webcam is working?
faq.a: If you see your own live picture after you allow the camera, the camera works in that browser. The test also reports the resolution and frame rate. A black or frozen picture usually means the camera is blocked, in use by another app, or covered.

faq.q: How do I check if my laptop camera is off?
faq.a: A camera that is off shows a black or blank picture. Look for a shutter or a cover over the lens, check for a key that switches the camera off, and make sure no other app is holding it. Then allow the camera for your browser and reload the test.

pages.title: Webcam Test on Windows 11: Check Your Camera Free | Lazur
pages.description: Test your Windows 11 webcam in Settings, then check the picture a website gets in your browser. Steps and fixes for a black screen. Free, no sign-up.
pages.claim: Open Start, then Settings, then Bluetooth & devices, then Cameras, and select your camera to see its preview. Then open this webcam test in your browser to check the picture a website gets. Free, no app, no sign-up.

sections.heading: Check the camera in Windows 11 Settings
sections.body:
Start with Windows. It shows whether the camera is connected and whether Windows can show its picture.

1. Select Start, then Settings.
2. Select Bluetooth & devices, then Cameras.
3. Under Connected cameras, select your camera.
4. The camera's page opens with a preview. If you see your picture, Windows can use the camera.

If your camera is not listed, Windows may not see it. Check the cable, or unplug a USB camera and plug it in again, then open the Cameras page once more. Microsoft's full guide is [Manage cameras with Camera settings in Windows 11](https://support.microsoft.com/en-US/windows/hardware/camera/manage-cameras-with-camera-settings-in-windows-11).

sections.heading: Test the picture in your browser
sections.body:
Windows shows the camera inside the system. The [webcam test](https://webcam-test.lazur.app/windows-11) shows the picture a website gets from the same camera. Open the page in your browser, select Allow when it asks for the camera, and check the live picture. If you have more than one camera, pick the one you want from the list.

**Compare the two results.** If the Settings preview and the browser picture show the same camera, your choice is set. If they show different cameras, pick the right one in the browser list and test again.

sections.heading: Allow camera access
sections.body:
Windows can block the camera for every app, and each app can be blocked on its own. Go to Settings, then Privacy & security, then Camera, and make sure camera access is turned on. Then check the app you use. Microsoft Teams, for example, appears as Microsoft Teams (work or school) in that list, and it must be turned on for Teams to use the camera.

After you change a setting, close the app or browser, open it again and run the test. Windows keeps the new setting the next time you open the app.

sections.heading: If the picture is black
sections.body:
Close any app that might be using the camera, such as Teams, Zoom or a browser tab on a meeting site. Then open the built-in Camera app: select Start, type Camera, and select it from the results. If the Camera app shows your picture, the camera works, and the problem is probably in the app or site you were using. Check the camera setting in that app.

If the Camera app also stays black, restart the PC, then check the Cameras page and the privacy setting again. A camera that stays black in every app may have a driver problem or a hardware fault, so try a different camera to find out.

While the Camera app is open, watch the picture for a few seconds. A picture that freezes or stutters can point to a driver or a loose connection rather than a setting, so note what you see before you change anything else.

faq.q: How do I test my webcam in Windows 11?
faq.a: Select Start, then Settings, then Bluetooth & devices, then Cameras. Select your camera under Connected cameras to see its preview. Then open the webcam test in your browser, allow the camera, and check the live picture in the browser too.

faq.q: How do I test if a webcam is working?
faq.a: Open the Camera app from Start, or the Cameras page in Settings, and look for a live picture. Then run the browser test. If you see yourself in both places, the camera works. A black picture usually means another app is using the camera or access is blocked.

faq.q: How do I check if my PC has a webcam?
faq.a: Open Settings, then Bluetooth & devices, then Cameras. A camera listed under Connected cameras means Windows can see it. Select the camera to open its preview, then check the live picture in the browser test.

faq.q: Why is my webcam not working on Windows 11?
faq.a: The usual causes are another app holding the camera, camera access blocked in Privacy & security, or the wrong camera selected. Close other apps, turn on camera access, pick the right camera and test again.

pages.title: Webcam Test for Zoom: Check Your Camera Before a Meeting | Lazur
pages.description: Check your webcam before a Zoom meeting: a live picture in your browser, then Zoom's own Video & effects preview. Free, no app needed for this step.
pages.claim: Open this webcam test to see your camera live in your browser. Then open Zoom's Settings, choose Video & effects, and confirm Zoom shows the same camera with a clear preview. Free, no sign-up for this check.

sections.heading: Check the camera here first
sections.body:
The browser test shows whether your camera works and gives you a live picture to compare with Zoom.

1. Open the [webcam test](https://webcam-test.lazur.app/zoom) and select Allow when the browser asks for the camera.
2. If you have more than one camera, pick the one you will use on the call.
3. Look at the picture for framing, light and focus, and note the resolution and frame rate the page reports.

If the picture is clear here, the camera works. Zoom keeps its own camera choice, so check that next.

sections.heading: Check the camera in Zoom's settings
sections.body:
Zoom has its own camera setting. Check it in the desktop app before you join:

1. Sign in to the Zoom desktop app.
2. Click your profile picture, then click Settings.
3. Click the Video & effects tab.
4. Check the preview. If it does not show the camera you want, open the camera list and choose that camera.

Zoom's help article is [Testing your video](https://support.zoom.com/hc/en/article?id=zm_kb&sysparm_article=KB0061836).

sections.heading: Check the camera during a meeting
sections.body:
You can test the camera in a meeting too. Start or join the meeting, click the up arrow next to the Video icon in the meeting controls, and click Video settings. If you do not see your video, open the drop-down menu under Camera and select a different camera.

Use this when the camera changes after you join, for example after you plug in a USB webcam or undock your laptop.

sections.heading: When this test and Zoom show different cameras
sections.body:
The browser and Zoom can pick different cameras. If the live picture here comes from your laptop camera and Zoom shows a USB webcam, choose the same camera in both places. Pick it in the list on this page, then choose it under Camera in Zoom's Video & effects tab.

Close other apps that might use the camera, then run both checks again. A clear picture in both places is what you want before you join. A browser tab on a meeting site can also hold the camera, so close those too.

sections.heading: Before the meeting
sections.body:
Run both checks a few minutes before the call, from the spot where you will sit. Use the same light and the same angle you will use on the call. If you want to check the camera without starting a meeting, see the [Zoom camera test page](https://webcam-test.lazur.app/zoom-camera-without-meeting).

Keep the Zoom window and the camera preview on screen for a few seconds. A picture that freezes or stutters in the preview is worth fixing before the call, because the other people will see the same problem. Close other video apps first, so the camera is free for Zoom.

faq.q: How do I test my webcam on Zoom?
faq.a: Sign in to the Zoom desktop app, click your profile picture, and select Settings. Open Video & effects and check the preview. If you do not see your camera, choose a different camera from the list.

faq.q: How can I test my webcam before a meeting?
faq.a: Open the webcam test in your browser, allow the camera, and check the live picture. Then open Zoom's Video & effects preview to confirm Zoom uses the same camera. A clear picture in both places means you are ready to join.

faq.q: Why is my Zoom camera black?
faq.a: Usually another app is using the camera, or Zoom has a different camera selected. Close other video apps and browser tabs on meeting sites, choose the right camera under Video & effects, and check the preview again. If it stays black, check camera access in your system settings.

pages.title: Zoom Camera Test Without a Meeting: 3 Free Ways | Lazur
pages.description: Test your camera in Zoom without a meeting: use the Video & effects preview, join Zoom's test meeting or run this free browser test. Steps inside.
pages.h1: Zoom test camera without a meeting
pages.claim: Yes. Open Zoom's Settings, choose Video & effects, and check the preview. No meeting is needed. You can also join Zoom's test meeting, or open this webcam test for a live picture with no Zoom account.

sections.heading: Option 1: the Video & effects preview
sections.body:
Zoom shows a live camera preview in its settings, and you do not need to start a meeting to see it.

1. Sign in to the Zoom desktop app.
2. Click your profile picture, then click Settings.
3. Click the Video & effects tab.
4. Check the preview. If the camera you want is not shown, choose it from the camera list.

This is the picture Zoom will send when you join, so it is the best check for Zoom itself. Zoom's help article is [Testing your video](https://support.zoom.com/hc/en/article?id=zm_kb&sysparm_article=KB0061836).

sections.heading: Option 2: Zoom's test meeting
sections.body:
Zoom has a test meeting that checks your camera, microphone and speakers. It is not a real meeting, and no one else needs to join. Zoom's help article [Joining a Zoom test meeting](https://support.zoom.com/hc/en/article?id=zm_kb&sysparm_article=KB0063307) explains how to start it. Open the Join Meeting Test page, click Join to launch Zoom, and follow the prompts to start the test meeting.

Use it when you want to check the camera and the audio in one place, inside Zoom.

sections.heading: Option 3: this browser test
sections.body:
Open the [webcam test](https://webcam-test.lazur.app/zoom-camera-without-meeting), select Allow when the browser asks for the camera, and check the live picture. It needs no Zoom account and no app. You can also choose a camera from the list, see the resolution and frame rate the page reports, and save a snapshot.

This test shows that the camera works in your browser. It does not show which camera Zoom uses, so run one of the Zoom checks as well.

sections.heading: Which option to use
sections.body:
Use the Zoom preview when you want to confirm the camera Zoom will use. Use the test meeting when you want to check the camera and audio together inside Zoom. Use the browser test when Zoom is not installed, or when you only need to know that the camera sends a live picture.

For a quick check, start with the Zoom preview. If it works, you are ready for the call.

sections.heading: Keep the test close to the call
sections.body:
A camera test is only useful if your setup stays the same. Test from the desk or chair you will use on the call, with the headset or microphone you will wear. Choose the same camera in every place you check. If you change your camera or move your laptop, run the check again.

If you use a headset, plug it in before you open Zoom, so the test uses the same audio device as your call. A test with the wrong device tells you little about the call.

faq.q: Can I test my camera without being in a meeting?
faq.a: Yes. The Video & effects tab in the Zoom desktop app shows a camera preview with no meeting. You can also use this webcam test in your browser, which needs no Zoom account.

faq.q: How can I test my camera before a meeting?
faq.a: Open the webcam test, allow the camera and check the live picture. Then open Zoom's Video & effects preview to confirm Zoom uses the same camera. A clear picture in both places means you are ready.

faq.q: How do I test my camera and microphone for Zoom?
faq.a: Join Zoom's test meeting to check both inside Zoom, since it covers the camera, microphone and speakers. You can also test the camera here and the microphone in [Mic Test](https://mic-test.lazur.app/) in your browser.

pages.title: Camera Test for Teams: Check Your Webcam Before a Call | Lazur
pages.description: Check your camera before a Microsoft Teams call with a live browser picture, then run Teams' own test call in Settings. No meeting needed. Free.
pages.claim: Open this webcam test to see your camera live before you join. Then open Teams' Settings, choose Devices, and select Make a test call to record and play back a short check. No meeting needed, and the browser test is free.

sections.heading: Check the camera here first
sections.body:
Start in the browser. It shows your live picture before you open Teams.

1. Open the [webcam test](https://webcam-test.lazur.app/camera-teams) and select Allow when the browser asks for the camera.
2. Pick the camera you will use in Teams, if you have several.
3. Check the framing and light, then take a snapshot if you want to compare later.

If the picture is clear, the camera works in this browser. Teams has its own camera check, so run that next.

sections.heading: Run Teams' own test call
sections.body:
Teams has a built-in check that records you and plays it back.

1. In the Teams desktop app, select Settings at the top right.
2. Select Devices.
3. Under Audio settings, select Make a test call.
4. Follow the Test Call Bot's prompts and record a short message.
5. Play it back, then review the summary to see how your camera, microphone and speaker performed.

You do not need to join a meeting. The test call is available only in English. Microsoft's help article is [My camera isn't working in Microsoft Teams](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/teams/meetings/my-camera-isn-t-working-in-microsoft-teams).

sections.heading: Teams on the web
sections.body:
The Teams test call is not available in Teams on the web. If you use Teams in a browser, use this webcam test to check your camera. For the built-in test call, open the Teams desktop app.

The browser test shows the picture the browser gets from your camera. The Teams test call shows how Teams handles your camera, microphone and speaker, so run both if you can.

sections.heading: What to look for in the test call
sections.body:
When the Test Call Bot plays your recording, watch the picture as well as the sound. Check that your face is in the frame, that the light on your face is even, and that the picture does not freeze or jump when you move your head. If the recording is dark, face a window or a lamp rather than sitting with a bright window behind you.

If the summary reports a camera problem, run the browser test again with the same camera selected. Then recheck the camera permission for Teams. Keeping the same camera and spot for every check makes the results easy to compare.

sections.heading: Camera permission for Teams
sections.body:
If Teams shows no picture, Windows may be blocking it. Go to Settings, then Privacy & security, then Camera. Turn on Microsoft Teams (work or school) in the list. On a Mac, open System Settings, then Privacy & Security, then Camera, and make sure Teams is selected.

After you change the setting, close all Teams windows, restart the computer and open Teams again. Then run the test call once more.

faq.q: Can you do a camera test on Teams?
faq.a: Yes. In the Teams desktop app, select Settings, then Devices, then Make a test call under Audio settings. The Test Call Bot lets you record a short message and play it back. You do not need to join a meeting.

faq.q: Can I test my camera on Teams without being in a meeting?
faq.a: Yes. The Teams test call does not need a meeting. Use Settings, then Devices, then Make a test call in the desktop app. On Teams on the web, use this webcam test in your browser instead, because the test call is not available there.

faq.q: How can I test my webcam before a meeting?
faq.a: Open this webcam test, allow the camera and check the live picture. Then run Teams' test call in the desktop app to confirm Teams uses the same camera and sounds clear. Both checks take only a few minutes.

faq.q: Why is my camera not working in Teams?
faq.a: The usual cause is camera permission. On Windows, turn on Microsoft Teams (work or school) under Settings, Privacy & security, Camera. Close all Teams windows, restart, and run the test call again.

pages.title: Webcam Test on Chromebook: Check Your Camera Free | Lazur
pages.description: Test your Chromebook webcam in Chrome with a live picture, then turn on camera access if it stays black. Free, no install, nothing uploaded.
pages.claim: Open this webcam test in Chrome on your Chromebook and allow the camera. If the live picture stays black, turn on camera access in Settings under Privacy and security, then allow the site. Free, no install.

sections.heading: Run the test in Chrome
sections.body:
Open the [webcam test](https://webcam-test.lazur.app/chromebook) in Chrome.

1. Select Allow when Chrome asks for the camera.
2. Check the live picture for framing and focus.
3. If you have more than one camera, pick the one you want from the list.
4. Take a snapshot if you want a still image to compare.

If the picture shows, the camera works and Chrome can use it.

sections.heading: Turn on camera access
sections.body:
If the picture does not show, check the Chromebook setting first.

1. Select the time at the bottom right.
2. Select Settings.
3. Select Privacy and security, then Privacy controls.
4. Turn on Camera access.

If your Chromebook has a physical camera switch, make sure it is on. Then reload the test page and allow the camera again.

sections.heading: Allow the site in Chrome
sections.body:
Chrome can block the camera for one site even when the Chromebook setting is on. To check, type chrome://settings/content in the address bar. Find the camera permission for the site and set it to allow. Then reload the page, select Allow when Chrome asks, and check the live picture again.

Google's help article is [Manage your camera and microphone settings](https://support.google.com/chromebook/answer/13128177?hl=en).

sections.heading: Use a USB webcam
sections.body:
A USB webcam is a good option if the built-in camera is poor or you use a desktop Chromebook with no camera. Plug the webcam in before you open the test, so it appears in the camera list. Then pick it from the list and check the live picture.

If the webcam does not show up, unplug it, wait a few seconds, then plug it in again into the same port. Try a different port if the first one does not work. Reload the test page after each change. Once the picture shows, choose the same webcam in the app you use for calls, so both checks look at the same camera.

sections.heading: Restart and close other apps
sections.body:
If the settings are right and the picture still does not show, restart the Chromebook and open the test again. Close any other app or tab that might use the camera, such as a video call app or a meeting site.

If the camera still does not work after these steps, contact the Chromebook maker or the camera maker, since the problem may be with the hardware.

A picture that freezes or stutters can mean the Chromebook is short on resources. Close tabs and apps you do not need, then test again. Note the setting you changed, so you can find it again after an update. If you write the steps down in order, the list is easy to hand to whoever helps you with the Chromebook later.

faq.q: How do I enable the webcam on my Chromebook?
faq.a: Select the time at the bottom right, then Settings, then Privacy and security, then Privacy controls, and turn on Camera access. Make sure any physical camera switch is on, then allow the camera for the site you use.

faq.q: How do I test if a webcam is working?
faq.a: Open this webcam test in Chrome, allow the camera and look for a live picture. If you see yourself, the camera works. If the picture stays black, check camera access in Settings and the site permission in Chrome.

faq.q: Will a webcam work on a Chromebook?
faq.a: Many USB webcams work on a Chromebook. Plug the webcam in before you open the test, then pick it from the camera list. If it does not appear or the picture stays black, check camera access, or try another camera.
